newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Korea Telecom sets US$100 million loan.
newsitem.headline: Korea Telecom sets US$100 million loan.

text.p: Korea Telecom is expected to close a US$100 million loan facility in early July, bankers said on Friday.
Korea Telecom, which is about 80 percent owned by the South Korean government, is a local and long distance telephone provider.
Bankers said the loan facility has a final maturity of seven years. Repayment is in nine equal semi-annual instalments after a three-year grace period.
The facility pays an interest margin of 45 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
Fees are 45 basis points for lead managers committing US$10 million, 40 basis points for co-lead managers committing US$5-9 million and 35 basis points for managers committing US$5 million.
ABN Amro, BZW Asia, Dresdner Bank, Kookmin Bank, Sakura Finance Asia, Sanwa Bank and BOT-Mitsubishi are arrangers.
In May, South Korea's Ministry of Finance and Economy said it planned to allow foreign ownership in Korea Telecom of 20 percent from 1998 and 33 percent from 2001.
It said it would limit individual foreign shareholdings in Korea Telecom to three percent.
